text:
elaine: FYI we got a DSAR erasure for user u-9a3. It covers chat logs, embeddings, and model traces. Also flagged: recent keystore snapshot vuln (CVE-2026-9999) may have touched archived snapshots. Need triage + delete plan. :eyes:

mike: ack. can you paste the request? legal/cust proof?

elaine: pasted the email to #legal DMed. Requestor provided ID and time window. They explicitly asked for full erasure (no retention exceptions claimed).

nina: if no legal hold, we should proceed. but because of CVE we might need forensics proof before deletion. legal wants a deletion receipt + evidence bundle.

raj: quick technical Q — embeddings are sharded across dedicated clusters and S3 snapshots. KMS rotates keys monthly. If snapshots encrypted under old keys, deletion must remove both DB rows and remove S3 objects (and update manifests).

mike: +1. snapshots may still exist in glacier class. We need a scoped purge job that: 1) marks records for erase 2) schedules S3 object deletion with lifecycle override 3) stamps audit events.

elaine: proposed sequence: 1) Freeze ingestion for u-9a3 to prevent new writes 2) run identification query to enumerate all artefacts 3) hold a forensics snapshot of current system state (hash + access logs) 4) perform deletion across DB, vector store, and S3 5) rotate access credentials used by deletion job 6) publish deletion receipt to user + legal.

sam: who owns step 3 (forensics snapshot)? we need a named owner to avoid delays.

mike: I can do the snapshot with help from sre-bot hooks. SRE will produce immutable logs and export a signed manifest.

raj: example query to find embeddings (we'll run locally):
```
SELECT id, shard, s3_key FROM embeddings WHERE user_id = 'u-9a3';
```
we should also list any cached prefix in the KV cache.

elaine: RBAC question: who can run the deletion job? right now devs in infra-admin can. we should limit to a short-lived service account and require 2 approvers for DSAR deletions (security + privacy).

nina: agree. privacy counsel must approve before destructive ops. also add an audit log entry with the DSAR ID and approver names.

mike: implementation note: deletion job should emit an HMAC-signed proof-of-deletion JSON blob that includes checksums and timestamps. store that in encrypted evidence bucket (KMS key separate from snapshots).

elaine: regarding KMS: because keys rotated, we need to ensure deleted S3 objects are removed even if re-encrypted by different keys. Use S3 delete marker + object-level deletion. Confirm with storage team if retention holds will block override.

mike: pinged @storage on that. storage team responded: "we can force-delete but need a retention-exception flag set by legal." If no retention, we can proceed.

nina: legal says no retention-exception on this user. proceed but hold the forensics bundle for 30 days in evidence bucket.

raj: vulnerability triage note: because of CVE, we should snapshot current keystore audit logs and include access token usage in the evidence bundle; escalate to SecOps if we see odd access.
